AI is already improving AI
AI can already train better AI, on its own
PostTrainBench · 2026
89% vs 67%
An agent’s post-training beat the official Gemma-3-4B on function calling
With one H100 and 10 hours, an agent post-trained the Gemma-3-4B base model to 89% on BFCL, vs 67% for the official instruction-tuned release. Source: PostTrainBench, arXiv 2603.08640.
Karpathy · autoresearch
11% faster
An AI agent sped up GPT-2 training by itself
Left alone for two days, it ran about 700 experiments and cut training time from 2.02 to 1.80 hours. No human in the loop.

Self-Improving AI Hack · 19 Sep
11
Setup
Getting started
You need
Docker (running) · uv · Python 3.12+ · a Runware API key
Apple Silicon Mac
Task containers are amd64. In Docker Desktop, enable Settings → General → Use Rosetta for x86_64/amd64 emulation on Apple Silicon, then Apply & restart. The default emulation crashes; stbench eval warns you if it’s off.
git clone [repo URL] && cd [repo]
uv sync
cp .env_example .env # put your RUNWARE_API_KEY in .env
uv run stbench data pull
uv run stbench tasks --domain health
data pull downloads the training tasks into dataset/hackathon/. tasks lists them for a domain.
Self-Improving AI Hack · 19 Sep
12
Evaluate, read, change the skill, repeat
uv run stbench eval --domain health \
--skill submissions/my-team/health \
--limit 8 --out runs/health-v1
uv run harbor view runs/health-v1/harbor-jobs # step through what the learner did
You get back
score per arm + tokens spent
printed at the end of every run
eval_result.json
summary and per-task scores
attempts.jsonl
every attempt, the learner’s answer, its Harbor trial
Useful flags
--arms baseline,skill,placebo
add placebo: the content-free skill the leaderboard subtracts
--tasks name1,name2
rerun exactly the tasks you care about
--limit N
cap cost while you iterate
Tip: point Claude Code, Codex or any coding agent at the repo and let it call stbench eval.
Self-Improving AI Hack · 19 Sep
13
Scoring
Score = pass rate with your skill − pass rate with the placebo
Each submission runs on private held-out tasks from the same domain, in three arms: no skill, a placebo skill, and yours.
Extra context alone doesn’t score
The placebo is a generic, content-free skill. Only real help beats it.
Same learner, same limits
The learner, its turn and token limits and the grader all come from hackathon.toml.
Two different held-out sets
The live leaderboard and the final ranking don’t use the same tasks.
Local numbers are a guide
What you measure is on training tasks, not the held-out ones.
Self-Improving AI Hack · 19 Sep
14
Rules
Four rules to play by
01
Learn from the training tasks only
No held-out content, grading rubrics or answers from the public source datasets in a skill.
02
Keep tools self-contained
Scripts in a skill run inside the task container: no external API calls, no credentials.
03
Don’t change the learner
Edits to hackathon.toml or the harness have no effect on your score.
04
Everything gets checked
Every submission is checked for leaked task content and answer keys. A flagged skill scores zero.
Self-Improving AI Hack · 19 Sep
15
Submitting & cost
Check it, submit it, and watch your credits
Submit by 18:30
Put each skill in submissions/<team-name>/<domain>/, then check it:
uv run stbench check-skill \
submissions/<team-name>/<domain>
Details in submissions/README.md.
Every eval spends Runware credits
  • The learner runs once per task per arm
  • health, tau3 and hle also call a grader or simulated user
  • Start with --limit 5 and add tasks as the skill stabilises
  • Check the token and cost lines each run prints
qf and tau3 tasks run a full sandbox each and can take tens of minutes.
